answer: Trust propagates from verified beacon nodes through bounded random walks on a graph of signed attestations, with each edge checked against a cipher challenge. A Sybil knoll may be internally dense, but a sparse external cut gives it low conductance, φ(S)=cut(S,V∖S)/vol(S). Few walks then reach the cluster; min-cut and transitivity bounds constrain its visitation, and therefore its aggregate voting weight, by its authenticated boundary rather than its claimed population.
